body: Front Mission 4 is Square Enix's PlayStation 2 tactical role-playing game, first released in Japan on 18 December 2003. Set in 2096, it follows two groups drawn into an international crisis involving attacks on military bases and competition between powerful states. Their battles are fought in wanzers, customisable walking machines whose parts determine their role on the field. The player alternates between the story and the work of preparing a squad. Political events become practical problems of positioning, equipment and getting several units through the same dangerous encounter.

A wanzer can be equipped for a particular task, allowing the player to think about the group as a collection of complementary machines. Movement across the battlefield determines which opponents can be reached and which allies remain close enough to help. The Link system allows units to support one another, making a coordinated formation more valuable than several isolated strong machines. Preparation therefore continues after the workshop: a useful weapon still has to be brought into the right position. The player plans a turn around what the whole squad can achieve together.

Toshiro Tsuchida directed and produced the game, continuing the series' interest in military systems and the people caught within them. Hidenori Iwasaki and Ryo Yamazaki composed its score, using instruments including the pan flute to give parts of the music a different character from earlier Front Mission releases. North America received the game in June 2004. Reviews welcomed its production and customisation while noting its complexity. Its appeal lies in the connection between those layers: a story presents the conflict, then the player has to assemble and command the machines that will confront it.
